# Vim OS JavaScript SDK [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#vim-os-javascript-sdk)

Welcome to the Vim OS JavaScript SDK documentation!

The Vim OS SDK is compatible with TypeScript and JavaScript, offering flexibility in your development environment. Healthcare EHR integration is made seamless with our SDK.

We reference Vim OS JavaScript SDK as "VimOS.js" in our documentation. Using VimOS.js in your application code allows you to easily integrate to the Vim middleware ecosystem and EHRs. If you want to enhance EHR workflows by bringing your applications to the point of care in the EHR while leveraging an engaging user experience, VimOS.js offers the tools and resources you need to seamlessly achieve your goal.

WARNING

The Vim API is only available for USA server-based instances (White listing IPs is **not** supported).

This means your application server must be hosted within the United States to access Vim's EHR connectivity features. If you are a developer accessing from outside of the US, you need to use a VPN to connect, but your app server must still be in the US for production use.

# Prerequisites​ [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#prerequisites%E2%80%8B)

Make sure you have the following prerequisites checked:

1. **Register for a Vim Canvas™️ developer account**: Sign up for a [Vim Canvas™️ developer account](https://console.getvim.com/organization-admin) to integrate VimOS.js into your code stack.

#### Note:

TIP

If you don’t have a Vim Canvas™️ developer account yet, please register [here](https://getvim.com/health-tech-innovators/?utm_source=sdkdocs) to request access.

2. [Create your first application](https://docs.getvim.com/testing/creating-application#create-your-canvas-application): Set up your application details and permissions.

3. [Get your developer keys](https://console.getvim.com/organization-admin/my-account): Obtain your developer client ID and secret keys to initialize the SDK and complete the authentication process.

4. [Access the Sandbox EHR](https://console.getvim.com/organization-admin/sandbox-ehr): Simulate how your application will works in Vim on EHRs.


# Install [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#install)

We provide two ways to incorporate VimOS.js into your application: Via a `script` tag in your `html`, and via a public `npm` package.

#### Script tag [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#script-tag)

Include the VimOS.js script on each page of your application to incorporate VimOS.js into your application. It should always be loaded directly from `connect.getvim.com` rather than included in a bundle or hosted yourself.

html

```
<head>
  ...
  <script src="https://connect.getvim.com/vim-os-sdk/v2.x.x/vim-sdk.js"></script>
  ...
</head>
<body>
  ...
</body>
```

#### tip

TIP

- If you are building a multi page application, you should include the script on each page of your application, not just the main page.
- Make sure to add the `script` tag before any script code that uses VimOS.js; this ensures VimOS.js is loaded when your code uses it.

#### NPM [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#npm)

We also provide an alternative method to incorporate VimOS.js with an [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/vim-os-js-browser) making it easier to load and use VimOS.js as a module. Using the `npm` package allows you also to leverage TypeScript powerful auto-completion capabilities. When working with TypeScript in an integrated development environment (IDE) such as Visual Studio Code, the IDE can use the type information defined in VimOS.js `npm` package to offer auto-completion suggestions.

To use VimOS.js as a module and leverage TypeScript auto-completion capabilities, you can install it in your tech stack like this:

npmyarnpnpm

bash

```
npm install vim-os-js-browser
```

bash

```
yarn add vim-os-js-browser
```

bash

```
pnpm add vim-os-js-browser
```

#### minimum requirements

INFO

VimOS.js TypeScript works with TypeScript V5 and above.

### Asynchronous and deferred loading of VimOS.js [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#asynchronous-and-deferred-loading-of-vimos-js)

Asynchronous loading of JavaScript is generally recommended, as it can improve your application user experience by not blocking DOM rendering during script loading. The easiest way to asynchronously load VimOS.js is to use the `npm` module. It does asynchronous loading by default.

Suppose you use the `script` tag method to integrate VimOS.js into your code stack. In that case, we recommend **not to set** the async attribute in the `script` tag, to ensure that VimOS.js is loaded synchronously before it is called in your application code, avoiding timing issues and ensuring that VimOS.js functions as expected.

If you prefer to load VimOS.js using the async or defer attribute on the `script` tag, you will need to make sure that any API calls to VimOS.js are made only after the script execution is completed. You can do so by checking for the existence of `vimSdk` on the window:

ts

```
  if (window.vimSdk) {
    ...
  }
```

### Next: Authentication, Vim EHR Connectivity and Vim Hub [​](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/setting-up\#next:authentication-vim-ehr-connectivity-and-vim-hub)

1. **[Authentication](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/authentication)**: Integrate your application securely to ensure authorized access to Electronic Health Record (EHR) resources and obtain access to the active session context.

2. **[Vim EHR Connectivity](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/vim-ehr-connectivity)**: Vim’s EHR-Connectivity gives you the ability to not only connect to the most popular EHRs, it allows you to leverage all its existing features and functionality such as read/write access to the EHR, workflow resources and their associated data. Additionally, any new features and functionality will be made available to you automatically.

3. **[Vim Hub](https://docs.getvim.com/vim-os-js/vim-hub)**: Vim Hub is the Vim Connect UI, which your users will experience when working in the EHR after you have built and deployed your application. Vim designed its Vim Hub features to provide an engaging and intuitive end-user experience that reduces administrative burden.
